text: Bed 12 is fine, Priya took him off the sepsis bundle at 0600 once the repeat lactate came back at 1.4. Still need the cultures repeated on bed 9 though, nobody charted them yet.

Dan, handoff for 4W is in the chart. Mr Okafor has a Morse score of 55 so bed alarm is on and I put in a sitter request. The pump in 14 is still an old Alaris, biomed said they would swap it Thursday.
Thanks for covering my last hour Marisol, I owe you a coffee. Tell Priya the BedBoard shows 2 dirty beds on the east hall and I already paged EVS.
Did the sweep at 2000, all call lights answered except 7 and 16. Alarms checked on the high falls. Census is 27 with one boarder from the ED.
Can someone grab the teach-back sheets from the Keisha binder? We have discharges at 1100 and I want the AVS printed before the family arrives.
Hollis from pharmacy called about the vanc level on bed 3, the trough is due before the 0800 dose not after. Pulled the order in Epic and held the dose until the lab draws.
Lunch was a disaster, nothing left in the break room and I am starving. Going to grab something from the cafe on 2 and be back by 1215.
Ruth wants the fall risk audit numbers by Friday, so I need every high-risk patient charted with the bed alarm documented. Only 11 of 19 are in compliance so far.
Quick question, is the 30 mL/kg bolus based on actual weight or ideal weight? The sepsis order set defaults to actual but the pump library says ideal.
Thanks Tomas for staying late on 9 and 10, you saved my night. Your pump charting was clean, Keisha will want to use it for the next teaching session.

Bed 22 went into a brady run around 0340, rapid response was called and he came back to baseline with the atropine. Family is now in the room. Please update the BedBoard before you pick up the next admission.
Float needed on 4W tomorrow. Ben is on the schedule for 3 patients, Marisol has the swing, can someone confirm with staffing before the huddle at 0645.

I do not love the new pump library, the Alaris drug list lets you pick concentrations we never stock. Filed a ticket with the smart pump team, the ticket number is in Epic under the pump safety folder.
Dan, the tele strip for bed 6 shows PVCs every few beats, I already told the cardiologist on call. Hold the metoprolol if the HR drops under 60 per the parameters.
Please remember the Q2 turns on the bariatric patient in 18, last charted turn was at 0100. Keisha says the wedge needs to be checked too.
Okay so the RN handoff tool is down again, I am writing everything on paper and will enter it into Epic when the system comes back up.
Bed 9 finished the cultures at 1030, two sets sent, one from each arm. The sepsis flag is still open on the BedBoard so do not clear it until the antibiotics are in.
Fall on 4W at 0215, pt in 16 got up to the bathroom without calling and slid down by the sink. No head strike, neuro checks normal, MD notified and x-ray ordered for the hip.
Ruth, staffing grid for next week is posted on the break room door. I am off Tuesday and Wednesday, I can pick up Sunday night if we are short.
Keisha ran the teach-back session on the new heparin protocol and only four of the eight nurses passed the quiz. We need to schedule a second round before the end of the month.
Marisol, the PICC on bed 5 is oozing a little at the dressing, changed it and reinforced with a gauze. Please keep an eye on it during your second round and let the team know if it continues.
Did the family in 12 understand the discharge instructions? They asked me twice about the metformin dose, can you go over it with them again when you get a chance.
Pyxis tub check for the east side is done, we were short two vials of the enoxaparin so I put in a restock request. Hollis said pharmacy will send them up on the 1400 run.
Honestly the sepsis reminder pop-up is driving me crazy, it fires every time I open the chart even when the lactate is already drawn. Priya said she would bring it up at the nursing council meeting.
Dan, all three of my patients are settled and the sitter is with the bed 16 gentleman. I am heading to the break room for ten minutes, text me if the rapid response team gets called again.
New admission in 8 is a 79 year old with CHF and a Morse score of 60. Put the bed alarm on, the non-skid socks are in the drawer, and the family said they would be in around 2000.
Pump swap on 4W is 14 of 22 done. Biomed is coming back Monday for the rest, please make sure the old Alaris units are tagged with the red sticker so nobody uses them by mistake.
Thanks for the coffee run, I owe you one. Can we move the huddle to 0700 instead of 0645 tomorrow? The overnight team wants to get out on time.
Ben is doing great on his first solo assignment, he caught a low sat on bed 20 before anyone else noticed. Give him a pat on the back at huddle if you see him, he is nervous.
Discharge teaching on the new insulin pen was not done for bed 4 before the patient left. Flagged it in the safety report and I called the patient at home to go over the steps.
The BedBoard is still showing bed 17 as occupied even though the patient went to CT at 0900. Someone needs to update the status or EVS will hold the room and the ED will keep boarding.
Sepsis bundle compliance on 4W is up to 78 percent this month, which is better than last quarter. Keep documenting the time zero in the flowsheet, the auditors look at that first.
I think we need a second bed alarm for the room 11 patient, he keeps trying to climb over the rail. Ask Priya if we can get one from the supply closet before the 1900 shift change.
Quick reminder that the fall risk huddle is Thursday at 1430 in the small conference room. Bring your bed alarm checklists and any close calls from this week so we can discuss them together.
Tomas, the family in 6 wants a pastor. I told them the chaplain is on call until 2300, and gave them the number at the desk. Can you help me find the spiritual care form in the chart?
Dan, the central line on bed 10 needs a dressing change, it was done at 0800 but the CLABSI checklist is not signed. Please sign it before the infection prevention rep comes around tomorrow.
Bed 19 is being discharged to a SNF at noon, the transport van is late so I told the family it would be around 1300. The AVS is printed and in the folder on the desk.
Staffing is short on nights again, Ruth approved two travelers for next week. One of them has done pump training before so she should be able to help Ben with the Alaris library.
My patient in 13 had a bowel movement after the senna, so I ran the cleanup and changed the linens. Still need to finish the I and O flowsheet before I hand off to Marisol.
Pump alarm on bed 7 kept going off all morning, it was a kinked tubing not a bad battery. Swapped the line and the pump is working fine now, but I flagged it so biomed can look at the set.
Heads up the EVS team is short today so the dirty beds are taking forever to turn over. If you need a room for a discharge, call the house supervisor directly and skip the queue.
Did you hear Priya is moving to days on the step-down unit next month? We will need a new charge on nights and Ruth wants recommendations by the end of the week.
Lactate came back at 3.8 on bed 2 so I started the 30 mL/kg bolus and called the team. Repeat lactate is due in two hours, I already added the order to the BedBoard task list.

Keisha wants everyone to use the new teach-back script for the heart failure patients, it is in the shared drive under the education folder. Please practice it on your next family discharge and note the response.
I know the huddle ran long, sorry about that. Summary is we have 3 falls this month, 2 sepsis cases, and the pump swap is behind. Priya will send the full notes to the group tonight.

Bed 15 pulled out the PIV again, the second one this shift. Restarted in the right AC, labeled the line and wrapped it with the purple tape so it is easy to see. Family says the patient gets agitated when the sitter leaves.

Hollis flagged a double dose of the heparin drip on bed 21 from the overnight order, the infusion rate was not adjusted after the aPTT came back. Corrected it and reported it in the safety system, the MD was called.
Ben asked me how to chart a fall without a head strike and I told him to use the post-fall huddle template. He did it perfectly, but he also wanted a second look at the Morse score which was right.
The old dressing cart on the west hall is out of gauze, I checked the supply room and it is empty too. Can you put in a request with central supply before the trauma patient comes up from the ED.

Pump library update went live at midnight, now the Alaris asks for the drug name before the rate. Took me three tries on the heparin, so give yourself extra time and do not force the screen if it looks wrong.

Okay the family in 8 wants a second opinion on the wound care plan, I told them the wound nurse can see them on Thursday. Please document their questions in the chart so the wound team has the full picture.
Sorry I was late this morning, the parking garage was full again and I had to walk from the lot on Elm. I did check the overnight notes and the bed 11 patient is still on the high fall protocol.

The new discharge teach-back flow is confusing for the patients who do not read English well, Marisol had a family in 4 who could not repeat the insulin doses back. Can we get the interpreter line on the forms?

Bed 18 finished the bowel prep and is resting now, the GI team will do the procedure at 0730. Keep the NPO sign on the door and remind the family they cannot have anything to eat or drink after midnight.
Quick question for you Dan, do you know if the sepsis timer resets after a fluid change or only after the antibiotics? The BedBoard flagged bed 9 again and I want to make sure I documented it right.

The sitter on the bed 16 patient is leaving at 1900 and nobody is covering for her yet. Staffing said the agency nurse will not arrive until after eight, so we need someone to stay until then or the alarm stays on.
Thanks everyone for the cards and the cookies this week, it means a lot to the whole unit. Ruth also wants us to sign the card for Keisha before she leaves on Friday.

Bed 11 patient fell in the bathroom at 0545, no injury found but he hit his hip on the toilet frame. Neuro checks normal, bed alarm was on but the cord was unplugged, I fixed it and reported the event for the falls audit.

Discharge on bed 20 went smoothly, the teach-back worked well with the daughter. She repeated the insulin pen steps without any help and asked for a copy of the sheet, so I printed one from the education folder.

Final handoff for the week: bed 9 has the sepsis flag open until the antibiotics are in, bed 16 has a sitter until 2300, and the new pump is in bed 14. Please check the BedBoard before you start rounds and tell Ruth if anything is still open.
